title: Mission Power Level Ceiling
doc: CKF Hard Mode - mission Power Level ceiling.
MissionPowerLevel = round( (TeamPowerLevel + offset) * scalar )
clamped to [MinCap, MaxCap]
This section does the one thing the game's own difficulty sliders cannot:
lift the ceiling of 10 the game clamps its own result to. Everything else -
the offset and the scalar - is set on the sliders, and read back off the
same GameDifficultyModel instance the postfix is handed.
SEVEN KEYS WERE REMOVED IN 2.12.0
and are now consts, because each was a measured fact about the game rather
than a preference:
DerivedCallMode        PassThrough. Run25 pinned arg0 to
max(1, Floor(teamPowerLevel)) across three saves -
the game handing its own standing back to itself,
which is a reward calculation and not a request for
a mission's difficulty. Recompute is the setting
that turned a reward of 1 into 2.
MatrixOffsetMode       Replace. Run21. The Matrix path uses
MatrixPowerLevelOffset INSTEAD of the base offset.
OffsetProperty         BasePowerLevelOffset  ) GameDifficultyModel's own
ScalarProperty         PowerLevelScalar      ) column names.
MatrixOffsetProperty   MatrixPowerLevelOffset)
InstanceTeamProperty   teamPowerLevel
TeamPowerLevelOverride deleted outright, not frozen - at its value of 0
the branch reading it was unreachable.
THERE IS NO FALLBACK SOURCE for Team Power Level. The database-discovery
machinery went in 2.11.0 (section 7.4). If the instance carries no readable
teamPowerLevel, or carries one that reads 0 - which a freshly constructed
model does before the game fills it in - this subsystem logs an error and
leaves the game's own result alone. It never proceeds on a default: a
default here is not a missing mission difficulty, it is a silently wrong one.
uiDoc: By default the game clamps mission to a PL of 10. Here, the upper clamp ships at 20 as enemy archetypes exist up to PL 20. The lower clamp must stay at or below the upper one; set it higher and this refuses to run at all.
Matrix calls have their own upper clamp, so hacking can have its own maximum difficultt. Set it to 0 to use the same clamp for both. Where the two differ, the lower one wins.
The count of logged calculations is also the gate on the check that the mod's Team Power Level agrees with the game's own. Set it to 0 and you lose that check along with the logging.

fields.label: Enabled
fields.doc: Recompute mission Power Level so it can exceed the stock ceiling of 10. 3.0 moved this switch and the four clamps out of the [PowerLevel] section of ckf.hardmode.cfg and into the "powerlevel" section of ckf.hardmode.json; the section is new in 3.0 and has no 2.x sidecar behind it, which is what targets.legacyJson: null records.

fields.label: Upper clamp
fields.doc: Upper clamp. Stock is 10; enemy archetypes exist through 20. Must not be below minCap - the subsystem refuses to run if it is.

fields.absent: 0 means use maxCap for Matrix calls too.
fields.label: Matrix upper clamp
fields.doc: Separate upper clamp for Matrix calls, so hacking can stay at the stock ceiling while ground missions climb. 0 = use maxCap for both. The lower of this and maxCap wins.

fields.label: Calculations logged
fields.uiDoc: Calculations to log. The cross-check that the mod's Team Power Level matches the game's own is printed inside this gate, so 0 silences the only check that the two agree.

invariants.reason: maxCap below minCap leaves nothing to clamp into; PowerLevelCap.Init logs an error and installs no hook. 3.0 moved both keys out of the cfg and into the merged document, so they are spelled file#path rather than Section.Key.
